Q5976.L1t: Homelessness statistics differ widely between countries because each uses its own definition of who counts as homeless.
Q5976.L2t: Cross-national comparisons of homelessness in 2013 relied on national counts that used differing definitions and methods.
Q5976.L3t: A single-night count in 2013 found roughly 600,000 homeless people in the country of about 315 million residents, a rate near 19 per 10,000, higher than the rates reported for the other listed countries.
Q5976.L4t: The United States had the highest per capita rate of homelessness of the four countries in 2013.
Q5976.L2f: Comparisons of homelessness in 2013 relied on a single standardized definition adopted by the United Nations and applied identically in every country.
Q5976.L3f: In 2013 the Iberian country reported the largest homeless population relative to its size, with a rate well above those of the other three countries.
Q5976.L4f: Spain had the highest per capita rate of homelessness of the four countries in 2013.

Q8413.L1t: The European Court of Human Rights interprets the European Convention on Human Rights, including Article 6's guarantee of access to a court.
Q8413.L2t: Al-Adsani was a dual British-Kuwaiti national who sued Kuwait in English courts over alleged torture, and the UK courts upheld Kuwait's claim of state immunity.
Q8413.L3t: The Court reasoned that the Article 6 right of access to a court is not absolute and may be limited, and that granting state immunity pursues the legitimate aim of complying with international law and promoting comity between states, making it a proportionate limitation rather than a breach.
Q8413.L4t: The Court found that recognising state immunity did not conflict with the right to a fair trial, so no violation was established.
Q8413.L2f: The Al-Adsani case concerned a commercial contract dispute between a British company and a foreign state.
Q8413.L3f: The Court treated the rule of sovereign immunity as overriding any competing Convention guarantee whenever the two clashed, resolving such a clash in favour of the state.
Q8413.L4f: The Court concluded that state immunity prevailed over the right to a fair trial where the two came into tension.

Q5601.L1t: Cross-national surveys regularly ask people how they view democracy and whether their governments serve citizens fairly.
Q5601.L2t: Surveys in 2019 asked respondents in many countries whether their state is run for the benefit of all the people.
Q5601.L3t: Turkey's figure in that survey was a clear majority of respondents, well above half, but short of three-quarters.
Q5601.L4t: About two-thirds of people in Turkey agreed that the state is run for the benefit of all the people.
Q5601.L2f: The 2019 survey in Turkey was carried out solely through face-to-face interviews with civil servants and asked mainly about trust in the courts.
Q5601.L3f: Turkey's result was well below half, with only about one in three respondents saying the state serves everyone rather than a narrow elite.
Q5601.L4f: Only about a third of people in Turkey agreed that the state is run for the benefit of all the people.
